projects.summary: You type or speak a request in a chat, and the server asks Llama 3.1 on Novita to turn it into a saved task shown on list and timeline screens.

ideaDistinctiveness.note: A chat-to-task manager; chat productivity assistants are the most common area in this field.

integrationDepth.note: A real Novita LLM call, task saving and recurrence projection are in code. Update and delete by chat, the interval and user separation are missing; no tests.

sponsorCentrality.note: Chat handling, the LLM call, storage and recurrence all run in Serverpod endpoints; the app is a thin client.

sponsorEvidence.note: Code only: the app's 9 calls trace to endpoints, but the demo is private and the Cloud link returns 404.

idea.description: A spoken-style request becomes a dated, prioritised task shown on a schedule.

evidence.note: The user talks to Butlr like an assistant.

refs.detail: “You can say: "Hey Butlr, remind me to check the oven in 20 minutes”

evidence.note: Plain language is turned into tasks, with no menus.

refs.detail: “Butlr turns raw natural language into structured, actionable tasks.”

evidence.note: The team names Llama 3.1-8B on Novita with a JSON-mode prompt wrapper.
Tasks get priorities from sentiment and keywords, and can recur (e.g. bi-weekly).

refs.detail: “Automatically calculates priorities based on task sentiment and keywords.”
“Parsing "next Tuesday" or "bi-weekly" requires the AI to have accurate state consciousness.”

evidence.note: Serverpod provides the ORM and client–server communication to PostgreSQL.

refs.detail: “Serverpod served as our "missing server for Flutter," providing a robust ORM”

evidence.note: A grouped list view, a timeline view and a current-time indicator.

refs.detail: “Offers a smart, grouped list view and a high-fidelity timeline view.”

evidence.note: The team says the server time and locale go into every prompt.

refs.detail: “We had to carefully inject the current server time and locale into every prompt”

evidence.note: The prompt wrapper is said to make the model return a valid schema.

refs.detail: “We implemented a custom JSON-mode prompt wrapper that ensures the model returns strictly valid schema.”

integration.description: The chat screen calls a Serverpod endpoint that prompts Llama, saves tasks and serves them to views.

evidence.note: The app sends the typed text to chat.processMessage. The mic fills the text box using on-device speech_to_text.
On the server it saves a task for 'create' and returns 5 open tasks for 'list'/'query'. It has no branch for update or delete.
AIService posts to Novita's chat completions with llama-3.1-8b-instruct. If JSON parsing fails, it falls back to keyword rules.
getTasks returns every task in the table. The code comment says user filtering is left for later.

refs.detail: // For now, get all tasks. In production, filter by user ID

evidence.note: getTasksByDate adds copies of daily, weekly, monthly and yearly tasks. The match never reads recurrenceInterval.

refs.detail: return diff % 7 == 0; // matches same day of week

evidence.note: The list groups tasks into Overdue, Today, Tomorrow and Upcoming. The timeline inserts a red now line and redraws every minute.
The prompt includes the server's current date and time and the last 10 messages. No locale or time zone is passed.

refs.detail: final history = await getChatHistory(session, activeSessionId, limit: 10);

evidence.note: The keyword list lives in the prompt text. The code only maps the model's 'high'/'low' strings, and anything else becomes medium.
recurrenceInterval is stored, but the weekly match is diff % 7 == 0 regardless of the interval.

refs.detail: return diff % 7 == 0; // matches same day of week

mapping.label: Edit by chat → create & list only

evidence.note: The prompt allows update and delete intents, but processMessage acts only on create, list and query.
The writeup lists voice as a next step, but the chat screen already dictates into the text box with on-device speech_to_text.

refs.detail: “True Voice-First Integration: Using Whisper or similar STT models”

questions.question: The writeup mentions 'bi-weekly', and the model returns a recurrence interval. Where does the schedule use that interval, so a bi-weekly task skips alternate weeks?
questions.basis: _matchesRecurrence checks only daily/weekly/monthly/yearly (weekly = diff % 7 == 0) and never reads recurrenceInterval, although processMessage stores it on the Task.

refs.detail: return diff % 7 == 0; // matches same day of week

questions.question: The prompt gets the server clock's date and time but no user time zone. On Serverpod Cloud, how does '9 AM' or 'in 20 minutes' match the user's local time?
questions.basis: L019 says server time and locale go into every prompt. _buildPrompt uses DateTime.now() on the server for date and HH:mm only, and chat_endpoint builds dueAt from those values on the server.

refs.detail: “inject the current server time and locale into every prompt”
dueAt = DateTime(date.year, date.month, date.day, hour, minute);

questions.question: If a user says 'move the dentist to Friday' or 'delete that', the model can return update or delete. What happens to the task?
questions.basis: The prompt lists update and delete intents, and TaskData is built for update. processMessage has branches only for create and list/query, so it would just reply with the model's text.

questions.question: The 'Try it out' link returned 404, and the demo video is private. Is there another way to see the Serverpod Cloud deployment running?
questions.basis: L024 claims a production deployment. main.dart targets butlr1.api.serverpod.space in release builds, and the web build uses base-href /app/. No source available here shows it responding.

refs.detail: “we successfully deployed a full-stack Dart application to a production cloud environment”

projects.title: The Bolt Chef
projects.creator: Laura Bolade, Dipo Onakunle
projects.summary: You write a note, attach an audio file or image, and tap Cook Insight; a Serverpod server sends it to Gemini and saves the summary reply.

ideaDistinctiveness.note: An AI note summariser with audio transcription; productivity assistants are the field's most common area.

integrationDepth.note: A real Gemini call with audio and image works in the demo; there are 6 endpoint methods, 2 tables, no auth, no tests, and Redis is off.

sponsorCentrality.note: All storage and the Gemini call run in Serverpod endpoints; the app is a thin client.

sponsorEvidence.note: The demo's '[Transcribed]:' text and SUMMARY label trace to endpoint code; the demo's processing bar is not in the code.

idea.description: A note of text, voice or image is 'cooked' by Gemini into a summary with tasks.

evidence.note: The user captures quick thoughts, voice recordings or brainstorm images.

refs.detail: “Whether it's a quick text thought, a voice recording from a long day, or an image of a brainstorm, Bolt Chef accepts it all.”

evidence.note: The note is called a Dish and can hold text, audio and images.
Gemini 2.5 Flash-lite summarises, finds tasks and transcribes audio.

refs.detail: “Integrated Gemini 2.5 Flash-lite (Very cost effective) to provide instant "Chef Insights.”

evidence.note: One tap on Cook Insight returns a summary and a list of Tasks Identified.
PostgreSQL stores the data and Redis is named for caching.

refs.detail: “PostgreSQL for reliable data storage and Redis for high-performance caching.”

integration.description: The Flutter app calls a Serverpod endpoint that sends the note to Gemini and saves the reply.

evidence.note: The demo shows the note editor, an audio file picker and a progress bar while the file is processed.
The server-side analyzeNote loads the note and returns a 'mock' insight if no Gemini key is set.
The server sends the prompt, audio bytes and saved image to gemini-2.5-flash-lite. A transcript appears at 37 s.
Two tables: note and ai_insight. Redis is disabled in the development config.
The demo shows the sheet with a saved SUMMARY. Its regenerate button calls analyzeNote with no audio.
The editor's Cook Insight passes the attached audio bytes to analyzeNote. The note must already be saved.
The server appends the reply to the note as '[Transcribed]:' and saves the insight with type 'summary'. At 37 s the prefix appears.
getInsightsForNote returns a note's insights ordered by newest createdAt.

mapping.label: Voice notes → audio file sent to Gemini

evidence.note: A 52.9 MB .wav is picked at 22 s, and a transcript with the '[Transcribed]:' prefix appears at 37 s.

mapping.label: Task extraction → free text in reply

evidence.note: Tasks come only from the prompt line 'Identify tasks if any'. The reply is saved as one text field.
Redis is set to enabled: false in the development and production configs.

mapping.label: List insight → text & image, no audio

evidence.note: The list's sheet calls analyzeNote without audio. The server takes audio only from that parameter, so Gemini gets the text and any image.

refs.detail: Future<AIInsight> analyzeNote(Session session, int noteId, {ByteData? audioData}

questions.question: The 'Processing audio file...' bar at 28 s does not appear in the repository's editor code. Was the demo recorded from the submitted code?
questions.basis: In note_editor_screen.dart, _pickAudio only attaches the file and shows 'Audio file attached. Click Cook Insight to analyze.' The string 'Processing audio file...' is not in the excerpts. The frame at 28 s shows that bar.

refs.detail: const SnackBar(content: Text('Audio file attached. Click Cook Insight to analyze

questions.question: 'Tasks Identified' is part of Gemini's free-text reply, saved as one string. Is there any structured task list that a user can track or complete?
questions.basis: L013 says the insight extracts specific tasks. The prompt only says 'Identify tasks if any', and AIInsight stores a single insightContent string with type 'summary'. At 37 s, the tasks section says 'None'.

questions.question: The writeup names Redis for caching, but Redis is disabled in every run-mode config. What was Redis meant to cache?
questions.basis: L010 says 'Redis for high-performance caching'. The redis section is enabled: false in the development, production, staging and test configs.

questions.question: getAllNotes returns every note in the table, and the app never sets userId. How would two users' notes be kept apart?
questions.basis: No NoteEndpoint method reads the session's user, and getAllNotes has no filter. _saveNote builds a Note without userId. main.dart opens the note list directly, with no sign-in screen.

projects.title: mamaCare
projects.creator: Fredrick Kioko
projects.summary: You enter a pregnancy profile, then log check-ins, kick counts and ultrasound photos; a Serverpod server asks Gemini for assessments.

ideaDistinctiveness.note: A maternal health tracker with AI check-ins; health apps already appear several times in this field.

integrationDepth.note: 23 endpoint methods over 6 tables, and Gemini output is seen in the demo; kick week is hard-coded, SOS is not traced, and there are no tests.

sponsorCentrality.note: Profiles, check-ins, kicks, scans, medications and every Gemini call go through Serverpod endpoints.

sponsorEvidence.note: All 20 app calls trace to endpoint code and the demo outputs match it; the server runs on a LAN address.

idea.description: A maternal health app that sends a mother's data to Gemini and handles reminders and SOS.

evidence.note: The tagline presents the app as a maternal health assistant for Kenyan mothers.

refs.detail: “MamaCare Butler is an AI-powered maternal health companion that provides:”

evidence.note: The writeup lists check-ins, ultrasound, kick counter, medications, SOS, trends and profile as features.

refs.detail: “Built comprehensive maternal health tracking - from daily medications to emergency SOS”

evidence.note: Gemini is said to analyse symptoms and vitals, ultrasound images and kick patterns.

refs.detail: “Gemini AI analyzes symptoms and vital signs to detect pre-eclampsia, gestational diabetes, and other high-risk conditions”
“Gemini Vision extracts measurements from ultrasound images”

evidence.note: The tagline names WhatsApp reminders; the writeup describes scheduled medication reminders.

refs.detail: “Comprehensive medication management with scheduled reminders for prenatal vitamins, iron tablets, and prescriptions”

evidence.note: Emergency SOS is said to send SMS with GPS to contacts and local hospitals.

evidence.note: Charts of blood pressure, weight and fetal movements with period filters.

integration.description: A Flutter app calls six Serverpod endpoints that store data in Postgres and call Gemini.

evidence.note: The dashboard with week, due date, quick tiles and SOS is shown; the client points at a local network address.

After a medication is saved, the app schedules one local notification per reminder time.

questions.question: The tagline promises WhatsApp reminders and the built-with list names Africa's Talking. Which code sends a WhatsApp or SMS message through either service?
